user.title: Menstruation Cycle
user.description: Create a profile (username + friendly name) for cycle tracking.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure profile
reconfigure.description: Update this profile's display name, icon, or onboarding stage. For all other settings (notifications, visibility, life stages, ...), use the integration's Configure/Options dialog instead.

error.invalid_profile: Profile must contain letters or numbers.

init.title: Menstruation Cycle Settings
init.description: General settings. Enable any life stages below to configure their details on the next screen(s).

data.birth_date: Birth date (YYYY-MM-DD, optional — enables age display and improves pre-menarche mode)

data_description.period_duration_days: Number of days the period typically lasts (1–14).
data_description.cycle_length_override: Override the automatically calculated average cycle length. Set to 0 to use the auto-calculated value from your history (recommended). Set to 20–38 to manually fix the cycle length used for fertile window and ovulation calculations.
data_description.num_predictions: How many future cycle starts to generate (1–12). Default is 6.
data_description.onboarding_stage: Choose pre-menarche, early menarche learning phase, or established cycle.
data_description.dashboard_enabled: Adds an optional dedicated Cycle Dashboard page to the Home Assistant sidebar.
data_description.calendar_enabled: Creates a native calendar.profile_cycle entity with predicted period, fertile window and ovulation events, usable in Home Assistant's own Calendar dashboard and calendar.* automation triggers. Disable if you don't need it - the same events remain available via the separate ICS feed export.
data_description.nfp_analysis_mode: Controls how ovulation and the fertile window are calculated. 'hybrid' (default) learns from observed temperature data and falls back to the statistical formula. 'strict' only shows ovulation and the fertile window when a temperature rise is confirmed in the current cycle.
data_description.pregnancy_enabled: Activates pregnancy tracking mode and shows a details screen next.
data_description.pre_menarche_enabled: Track puberty signs before the first period (menarche) and shows a details screen next.
data_description.menopause_enabled: Activates menopause tracking mode and shows a details screen next.
data_description.postpartum_enabled: Activates postpartum tracking mode and shows a details screen next.
data_description.notifications_enabled: Sends a notification when the period is predicted to start tomorrow, or when the fertile window starts today.
data_description.notify_service: Home Assistant notify target to use. Leave empty to use a persistent notification (shown in the HA UI) by default.
data_description.linked_person_entity_id: Link this profile to an existing person (Settings → People). If that person has a picture, the companion app can show it as the profile picture.
data_description.visibility_level: Controls how much of this profile's data appears in sensor attributes (dashboards, cards, and the companion app's overview screens). 'Full' (default) shows everything as before. 'Status only' shows just coarse, prediction-near values (next period / current phase), no symptom or health details. 'Private' shows almost nothing beyond the fact that the profile exists. Applies only to sensor attributes — services called directly (e.g. get_full_history) are unaffected, since the integration has no way to distinguish which device or person is calling.
data_description.notify_period_enabled: Sends a notification a configurable number of days before the period is predicted to start. Requires 'Enable notifications' above.
data_description.notify_period_lead_days: How many days ahead of the predicted period start to notify (0–7). 1 (default) means the day before, 0 means the same day.
data_description.notify_fertile_enabled: Sends a notification a configurable number of days before the fertile window is predicted to start. Requires 'Enable notifications' above.
data_description.notify_fertile_lead_days: How many days ahead of the predicted fertile window start to notify (0–7). 0 (default) means the same day.
data_description.temperature_unit: Which unit basal_temp values are interpreted in when logged via the log_symptoms/add_symptom service. Storage and the basal-temperature sensor always stay in Celsius — Home Assistant automatically displays it in the unit your HA instance is configured for.

data.pregnancy_risk_notes: Risk notes (optional, e.g. condition or monitoring focus)

data_description.pregnancy_start_date: First day of last menstruation (LMP). Leave empty to use the last recorded cycle start.

data_description.family_menarche_age: Age of menarche in the family (mother/sister) used to estimate the expected age.

data_description.menopause_start_date: Date when menopause started (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty if unknown.

data_description.postpartum_start_date: Date the baby was born. Used to calculate the postpartum tracking window.
data_description.postpartum_duration_days: How many days after birth to stay in postpartum mode (1–365). Default is 42 (6 weeks).

confirm.title: Review and confirm

error.invalid_date: Invalid date format. Please use YYYY-MM-DD.
error.invalid_menarche_age: Age must be a number between 8 and 20.

log_product_usage.name: Log product usage
log_product_usage.description: Log period-product usage for timer integrations and long-term statistics.

action.name: Action
action.description: Usage action, for example used or emptied.

quantity.name: Quantity
quantity.description: How many products or emptying events to add.

date.name: Date
date.description: Optional ISO date to backfill. Defaults to today.

reimport_basal_temp_statistics.name: Re-import basal temperature statistics
reimport_basal_temp_statistics.description: Force a fresh import of historical basal-temperature readings into Home Assistant's long-term statistics. Normally runs once automatically; use this to retry if an earlier attempt found nothing.

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: Target basal-temperature or menstruation gauge sensor.

get_full_history.name: Get full history
get_full_history.description: Retrieve the complete, uncompacted symptom history (and product usage) for a profile, bounded to a number of recent days. Bypasses the sensor's attribute size limits, which can drop symptom_history entirely under heavy tracking history.

days.name: Days
days.description: How many recent days to include (1-730). Defaults to 180.

get_cycle_predictions.name: Get cycle predictions
get_cycle_predictions.description: Retrieve fertile window and ovulation day estimates for past and future cycles, not just the current one — the same per-cycle estimate the calendar card already shows for every cycle displayed.

days_back.name: Days back
days_back.description: How many days of past cycles to include (1-1825). Defaults to 365.

future_cycles.name: Future cycles
future_cycles.description: How many future cycles to project forward (0-24). Defaults to 3.

export_full_backup.name: Export full backup (all profiles)
export_full_backup.description: Write a single JSON file containing the complete stored data (history, symptoms, product usage, pregnancy/menarche/menopause/postpartum data, ...) for every configured profile — for backup purposes, not just one profile's cycle-start dates like export_history. The calendar-feed token is intentionally left out of the export for security.

filename.name: Filename
filename.description: Base filename (without extension) to save under. A timestamped name is generated automatically when left empty.

import_cycle_history.name: Import cycle history (from another app)
import_cycle_history.description: Additively imports cycle-start dates — unlike set_cycle_history, existing history is kept, not replaced. Tolerates ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and dotted (DD.MM.YYYY) dates automatically; slash-separated dates are only parsed when date_format is explicitly set, since day-first vs. month-first is otherwise ambiguous. Dates that can't be parsed are skipped and reported back rather than aborting the import.

dates.name: Dates
dates.description: List of date strings to import, in ISO, dotted, or (with date_format set) slash format.

date_format.name: Date format
date_format.description: How to interpret slash-separated dates: 'auto' (default) only accepts ISO/dotted dates, 'dmy' treats DD/MM/YYYY as day-first, 'mdy' treats MM/DD/YYYY as month-first.

import_full_backup.name: Import full backup (all profiles)
import_full_backup.description: Restores data from a file previously written by export_full_backup. Only restores into profiles that are already configured (matched by profile slug) — never creates a new profile. Mode 'merge' (default) only fills in gaps and never overwrites data you already have; mode 'overwrite' fully replaces a matched profile's data with the backup's contents. Requires confirm: true.

filename.name: Filename
filename.description: Name of the backup file to read, from the menstruation_cycle_exports folder (without path).

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: 'merge' only fills in missing data without overwriting anything existing. 'overwrite' fully replaces a matched profile's data with the backup.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be set to true to confirm this write operation.

repair_storage.name: Repair/diagnose storage
repair_storage.description: Read-only diagnostic across every configured profile's stored data. Reports where normalization silently discarded or reset an invalid value (e.g. an out-of-range cycle_length_override, an unrecognized onboarding_stage or visibility_level, unparsable history/symptom/product-usage entries) as well as semantic inconsistencies (e.g. pregnancy_data marked active without a start_date, or pregnancy and menopause both active at once). Changes nothing.

migrate_config_entry.title: Menstruation Cycle: Integration Migration Required
migrate_config_entry.description:
The **{old_domain}** integration has been renamed to **{new_domain}**.

Profile: **{entry_title}**

Your sensor data and history will be preserved after migration. Click **Fix** to complete the migration.

rename_entities.title: Menstruation Cycle: Entity ID naming update available
rename_entities.description:
Profile: **{entry_title}**

The following entities still use an older ID scheme from before this integration started prefixing entity IDs with `menstruation_` for easier searching:

{renames_list}

Renaming keeps all history and statistics intact, but **any dashboards, automations, or scripts referencing the old entity ID(s) will need to be updated manually** afterwards. Click **Fix** to rename them, or dismiss this issue to keep the current IDs.

stale_ics_token.title: Menstruation Cycle: Calendar feed token hasn't been rotated in a while
stale_ics_token.description:
Profile: **{entry_title}**

The calendar-subscription (ICS) URL for this profile still uses a token that's about {age_days} days old. Anyone who ever had that URL (an old device, a shared calendar, a screenshot, ...) can still use it to read this profile's predictions, since the feed has no separate login. Click **Fix** to generate a fresh token — existing calendar subscriptions will stop working and need to be re-added with the new URL — or dismiss this issue to keep the current one.

low_prediction_confidence.title: Menstruation Cycle: Predictions are still low-confidence
low_prediction_confidence.description:
Profile: **{entry_title}**

This profile has {valid_cycles} of the {min_valid_cycles} recent cycles needed for high-precision predictions - fertile window and ovulation dates are still rough estimates. This isn't an error, just a normal part of getting started: predictions automatically become more precise the more cycles you log. No action needed here; dismiss this issue if you'd rather not see it while you're still building up history.
